source.author: verg
source.text: Qualis spelunca subito commota columba, cui domus et dulces latebroso in pumice nidi, fertur in ana volans, plausumque exterrita pennis dat tecto ingentem, mox aere lapsa quieto radit iter liquidum, celeres neque commovet alas:
source.text_original: Qualis spelunca subito commota columba, / cui domus et dulces latebroso in pumice nidi, / fertur in ana volans, plausumque exterrita pennis / dat tecto ingentem, mox aere lapsa quieto / radit iter liquidum, celeres neque commovet alas: /
source.text_english: As when a dove, suddenly disturbed in her cave, to whom is a home and sweet nests in a sheltering rock, flies out into the air and, frightened, beats a great flap of her wings against the roof, then, gliding down through the calm air, skims her liquid course and scarcely stirs her swift wings:

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: numquid , quia graui corpore terrae haereo, auium non miror uolatus nec columbam praedico, quod radit iter liquidum celeris neque commouet alas?
reuse.text_original: numquid , quia graui corpore terrae haereo, auium non miror uolatus nec columbam praedico, quod radit iter liquidum celeris neque commouet alas?
reuse.text_english: What then, because I cling to the earth with a heavy body, do I not marvel at the flight of birds, nor praise the dove because, swift, she skims the liquid air and does not stir her wings?
